hook_text: From space you can trace exactly where the gold was found under Johannesburg. Look for the pale yellow line.
clip_script: A satellite picture has no labels, so you read it like a detective. Clue one: colour. Clue two: texture. Clue three: shape. People make straight lines and circles; nature makes wiggles. Now zoom into Johannesburg. Running east to west is a line of pale yellow, flat-topped shapes. They are not clouds and they are not salt pans. They are old gold mine dumps, crushed rock left behind after the gold was taken out, piled up along the exact line of the gold reef discovered in 1886. The geology is hidden underground, but the mining traced it on the surface for us. Now zoom out to the Northern Cape: bright green circles in brown desert, fields watered by sprinkler arms swinging round in circles beside the Orange River. Two clues, one story: people shape the land, and the satellite sees it all.
visual_style: A whiteboard satellite view of Gauteng with a dotted pale-yellow line appearing east to west; then a pan to brown land dotted with bright green circles beside a winding river.
pacing: Clues first, the reveal over Johannesburg, a quick second case in the Northern Cape.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any satellite image like a detective.
